title: NG4: Pruning conditions (P)/(H) claimed necessary are not implied by (U) and (G) -- unsound pruning, Correctness proof fails

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, Algorithm section, paragraph "Pruning" (lines 298-304), relied upon by the Correctness proposition (lines 281-288).

**The gap (new; not covered by G1-G5 or NG1-NG3).** The pruning paragraph lists, as *necessary* conditions for geodeticity usable to reject candidates during backtracking:
- **(P)** every pentagon has odd total weight;
- **(H)** on every hexagon the two arcs of each 1+5 and 2+4 split have distinct weights;

and justifies them in one line: "These are special cases of (U) and (G) for branch pairs and branch targets." This justification is INVALID for (P) and for the 1+5 part of (H), so the conditions are not proven necessary, and using them to prune makes the algorithm UNSOUND.

**Why (P) is not necessary.** Inside a pentagon the only intrinsic uniqueness constraint comes from the two branch vertices u,w at pentagon-distance 2. By the Moore property (srg(50,7,0,1): any two non-adjacent vertices have a UNIQUE common neighbour) their unique common neighbour is the middle pentagon vertex, so their geodesic is the 2-arc of weight w2, with the 3-arc of weight w3 = T - w2 (T = pentagon total) the only competing within-pentagon route. Geodeticity requires w2 != w3, i.e. T != 2*w2. "T odd" forces this for every such pair and is therefore SUFFICIENT, but it is NOT necessary: an even total T violates uniqueness only if some 2-arc equals exactly T/2. A geodetic assignment may carry an even-total pentagon provided no 2-arc hits the half-split. Hence (U) and (G) do NOT imply (P).

**Why this is load-bearing.** The Correctness proposition states "the pruning discards only non-geodetic x, since the conditions used are necessary," concluding the algorithm "returns exactly {x : G'(x) geodetic}." If (P) is enforced as a prune, the algorithm can DISCARD genuinely geodetic assignments (even-total pentagon, no half-split), so the returned list is INCOMPLETE and the correctness claim fails. The 1+5 hexagon prune has the identical defect: a 1-arc = 5-arc coincidence forces non-geodeticity only when the single subdivided edge is actually the a-b geodesic; otherwise neither arc is minimal and rejecting the candidate is unjustified.

**Contrast.** The 2+4 hexagon condition IS genuinely necessary: for hexagon vertices at cycle-distance 2 the 2-arc is the (unique-common-neighbour) H-geodesic, so 2-arc = 4-arc yields a second minimum-weight H-path, a bona fide (U) violation. Only such (U)-derived splits (short arc = H-geodesic) and full (U) are safe necessary prunes.

**To close.** Either (a) PROVE (P) and the 1+5 (H) part are genuinely necessary -- which requires showing no geodetic assignment admits an even-total pentagon (a non-obvious global statement), or (b) demote (P) and the 1+5 condition to sufficient-only heuristics that may NOT reject candidates, retaining only the 2+4-type splits (short arc = geodesic) and full (U) as sound necessary prunes. As written, the Correctness proof is incorrect.
